patch_resolves_note: The fixed original reuses the same witness and still executes the protected `memcpy(out, repl, replSize)` event, but by moving `tempBuf` to loop scope it keeps the retained replacement pointer backed by live stack storage instead of an expired branch-local buffer.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-derived parsed document state and requests escaped serialization of an attribute child list. Passing `0` as `inLine` is what sends the data into the escaping logic that eventually reaches `xmlEscapeText()`.

Patch-relevant lifetime bug. `tempBuf` is declared only inside the `offset < 0` branch, so its lifetime ends at that branch's closing brace even though later code still uses a pointer derived from it. The fix moves this declaration to the top of the loop body.
ASan sink. `repl` still points to expired stack `tempBuf`, so this copy reads the serialized replacement bytes from out-of-scope stack storage.

nodes.state: In the `offset < 0` branch, `repl = tempBuf` makes the later copy source alias the branch-local stack buffer holding the serialized character reference.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable trace records `tempbuf_alias_assign.tempbuf_storage_ptr=0x7f2682c022a0`, the same pointer later retained after scope exit.

nodes.state: Immediately after control leaves the branch, `repl` still carries the same `tempBuf`-derived pointer even though the vulnerable branch-local storage is no longer live.

edges.evidence: In the vulnerable trace, `tempbuf_alias_assign.tempbuf_storage_ptr == stale_repl_after_scope.retained_repl_storage_ptr == 0x7f2682c022a0` with ordered event indices 0 -> 1.
In the vulnerable trace, `stale_repl_after_scope.retained_repl_storage_ptr == escape_memcpy_sink.repl_argument_ptr == 0x7f2682c022a0` with ordered event indices 1 -> 2.
